_note: Segment-driven model (as MEESHO/SWIGGY): each segment's NTV grows; revenue and adjusted EBITDA (company definition, after rent) are % of NTV. Reported EBITDA = Σ segment adjusted EBITDA + rent added back − KSA JV loss − ESOP. Valued on a sum of the parts on Sep-28E (roll FY28E/FY29E 50:50). ₹ crore.

segments.name: India consumer services (ex-InstaHelp)
segments._why: NTV +19% in FY26 and +29% in Q1FY27, the fourth quarter of acceleration (10% → 19% → 21% → 26% → 29%), helped by a rain-hit Q1FY26 base (+10%). Users +21%, spend per user +7%, Tier 2 cities +36%. Management gives no growth guidance. We use 24% / 20% / 18% (20.7% a year FY26-29E), close to Emkay (19.8%) and above Ambit (18%) and MOSL (17%).
segments._revWhy: Revenue was 34.3% of NTV in FY26 and 33.7% in Q1FY27 (commission, fees and B2B2C product sales to partners). We hold 34%.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA 4.1% of NTV in FY26 (3.3% in FY25) and 6.9% in Q1FY27 (+170 bp YoY; Q1 is the seasonal high). Steady-state target 9-10% "over the next few years". We assume +150 bp in FY27E (5.6%), then 6.8% and 7.8%: about 120 bp a year, below the pace of FY25-26 and short of the target by FY29E.

segments.name: International (UAE, Singapore)
segments._why: NTV +75% in FY26 and +76% in Q1FY27 (+58% in constant currency; the weaker rupee added ~18 pp). UAE demand fell 15-20% in late Mar-2026 with the Middle East conflict. We assume 50% / 35% / 28%.
segments._revWhy: Revenue 26.4% of NTV in FY26, 27.4% in Q1FY27; 27%.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive in FY26 (₹6 cr, 0.9% of NTV; 1.3% in Q1FY27), with contribution margin steady at 17-18%. Operating leverage lifts it to 1.5% / 3% / 4.5%; management wants growth over margins here.

segments.name: Native (water purifiers, smart locks)
segments._why: NTV +122% in FY26 and +51% in Q1FY27 (growth slowing from a small base); new purifier and lock models launched in Q1FY27. We assume 45% / 35% / 30%.
segments._revWhy: Revenue 77% of NTV in FY26 (products are sold, not commissioned) and 80% in Q1FY27; 79%.
segments._marginWhy: Loss narrowed from −25.1% of NTV (FY25) to −8.9% (FY26) and −7.3% (Q1FY27); management sees profitability "over the next few quarters". Rupee and commodity costs are a headwind. −5% / 0% / +3%.

segments.name: InstaHelp (on-demand house help)
segments._why: NTV ₹79 cr in FY26 (first year) and ₹53 cr in Q1FY27 (orders +43% QoQ to 3.8 mn; AOV ₹138 and falling). We assume ~20% QoQ growth through FY27 (₹288 cr), then +80% and +50%. TAM in the top 15 cities ₹7,000-12,000 cr (company).
segments._revWhy: Revenue 21% of NTV in FY26 and Q1FY27.
segments._marginWhy: Loss ₹235 cr in FY26 and ₹132 cr in Q1FY27 (₹346 an order). Management: investment for "the next 2 years, if not longer"; pricing has to rise from ~₹150 to ~₹200 an hour to break even, which may take "a couple of years" or five. We assume ~₹560 cr of losses in FY27E, ~₹480 cr in FY28E and ~₹380 cr in FY29E, so the group misses the Q3FY28 breakeven guidance by about a year.

_unallocLabel: Rent added back less KSA JV loss
_unallocWhy: Company adjusted EBITDA deducts rent (lease payments ₹38 cr in FY26, ₹11 cr in Q1FY27); Ind AS EBITDA does not, so we add it back: ₹46 / 52 / 58 cr. Screener's EBITDA includes the share of the KSA JV loss (₹31 cr in FY26, ₹5 cr in Q1FY27; the JV sees profit "in the coming quarters"): ₹15 / 5 / 0 cr. Net: −31 / −47 / −58 (negative = adds to EBITDA).
_esopWhy: ESOP cost ₹104 cr in FY26 and ₹38 cr in Q1FY27 (₹150 cr annualised) as post-IPO grants vest; 10 cr options outstanding. Non-cash, but it dilutes shareholders (counted in our 156.2 cr shares).
_capexWhy: Capex on equipment and offices ₹40 cr in FY26 (₹14 cr in Q1FY27), plus lease-principal repayments (₹26 cr in FY26) that we treat as capex because the engine adds rent back to EBITDA: ₹85 / 95 / 105 cr.
_depWhy: D&A ₹45 cr in FY26 on ₹236 cr of average gross block incl. right-of-use assets (19%); ₹16 cr in Q1FY27 (₹64 cr annualised) as new office leases started. 20% gives ₹62-81 cr in FY27-29E.
_treasuryWhy: Treasury income (bonds, bank and corporate deposits, mutual funds) ₹130.8 cr in FY26 (AR note 22) on ~₹1,930 cr of average company cash; the engine applies the yield to cash less lease liabilities (₹1,885 cr at Mar-26), so 7.2% on that base. FY27E other income ₹142 cr vs ₹137 cr in FY26 and ₹144 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26.
_otherIncomeWhy: Royalty from the KSA JV (₹3.1 cr) and other small items (₹2.8 cr) in FY26: ₹6 cr a year.
_interestWhy: Finance cost ₹12 cr in FY26 and ₹3 cr in Q1FY27, all lease interest; no borrowings.
_taxWhy: Statutory ~25% from FY29E, the first profitable year in our model; 0% in loss-making FY27-28E (no tax credit is booked on group losses, and setting 0% keeps the Excel model, which would otherwise book a credit, identical to ours). in practice profitable subsidiaries paid ₹8 cr in Q1FY27 while the group lost money (not modelled; a gap). ₹151 cr of deferred-tax assets remain and could be reversed further if InstaHelp losses persist.

otherTreasury.label: Fixed deposits held in other assets (treasury)
otherTreasury._why: Company cash & treasury investments ₹2,021 cr at Mar-26 (Q4FY26 letter) less ₹1,794 cr shown as cash and investments on Screener's balance sheet; the difference is deposits reported in other financial assets.

dcf._betaWhy: Long-duration, loss-making consumer-internet stock; 1.1 gives a 13.1% cost of equity, as for Eternal and Meesho. No debt beyond leases, so cost of equity = WACC.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~23% (FY29E) to 10% by year 15: online share of home services is still ~1%.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 22% reported EBITDA margin on revenue: India services at ~9% of NTV (the steady-state target) is ~26% of revenue; less ESOP, plus International and InstaHelp at lower margins.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. lease principal ~2% of revenue at maturity (FY26 4.2% of revenue on a small base).

parts.name: India consumer services (ex-InstaHelp)
parts.note: EV / one-year-forward NTV derived from the stock's own trading since 1-Nov-2025 × the internet sector's move over the same window (see the derivation table); one multiple for the whole core (India services, International, Native), applied to each part's Sep-28E NTV.

parts.name: International (UAE, Singapore)
parts.note: EV / one-year-forward NTV derived from the stock's own trading since 1-Nov-2025 × the internet sector's move over the same window (see the derivation table); one multiple for the whole core (India services, International, Native), applied to each part's Sep-28E NTV.

parts.name: Native
parts.note: EV / one-year-forward NTV derived from the stock's own trading since 1-Nov-2025 × the internet sector's move over the same window (see the derivation table); one multiple for the whole core (India services, International, Native), applied to each part's Sep-28E NTV.

parts.name: InstaHelp (losses still to fund)
parts.metricLabel: FY28E adjusted EBITDA (loss) × PV factor of losses to breakeven
parts.note: Start-up losses valued as the present value of the losses still to come after Mar-2027 (PLAYBOOK §7c): our path of ~₹480 / 380 / 250 / 100 cr in FY28-31E discounted at 13.1% (factor on FY28E). Bull: breakeven in FY30E; bear: ~₹480 cr a year for five years. Any value of a category winner is upside.

parts.name: Net cash at end-FY27E
parts.note: Model forecast: cash, deposits and treasury investments less lease liabilities at Mar-27.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: The street's method (JM Financial, Motilal Oswal, Kotak, Emkay): four businesses at different stages. The profitable core (India services, International, Native) on EV/NTV, the one yardstick we can derive from the stock's own short history; InstaHelp at the present value of its losses to breakeven; plus cash. Primary.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Whole-company cash flows over 15 years at a 13.1% cost of equity (Ambit and Emkay use a DCF); tests whether the NTV multiple is backed by a credible path to cash.

methods.name: EV/sales (Goldman Sachs)
methods.why: Goldman Sachs' disclosed yardstick: ~9x FY28E EV/sales. On our FY28E revenue it shows what the street's sales multiple implies.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India services grows ~25% a year (Q1FY27 pace holds) and reaches 9% of NTV by FY29E; International and Native grow faster; InstaHelp breaks even in FY30E; the market keeps the stock's own median multiple (no sector move).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: India services slows to ~15% growth (as in FY25-26) with margins stuck near 6% of NTV; the InstaHelp subsidy war deepens and losses stay near ₹600 cr a year for five years; the multiple falls to the stock's own 25th percentile × the sector move.
